title: Can a Spin Liquid State Persist as the Ground State in the Presence of Competing Interactions and Disorder?
abstract: In this report, we have shown that, in an otherwise geometrically frustrated lattice, the underlying interactions compete to stabilize different magnetic phases. In conjunction with fluctuations, these interactions may lead to the formation of unusual ordered phases, providing a pathway for understanding the fluctuation-driven order-by-disorder phenomenon. This competition is further modified by the presence of inherent structural disorder in a frustrated two-dimensional lattice. Furthermore, due to the local nature of the additional structural disorder, the majority of the samples evolve toward glassy dynamics, which can not only mimic spin-liquid-like behavior but also make it difficult to identify genuine spin-liquid candidates experimentally.
summary: This theoretical work examines the stability of spin liquid states in frustrated magnets under the influence of competing interactions and structural disorder. Using advanced field theory and the replica method, the authors show that disorder tends to suppress true long-range order, causing the system to enter a glassy state. This highlights the experimental difficulty in distinguishing genuine quantum spin liquids from disorder-induced glassy dynamics.
main_problem: The paper investigates whether a quantum spin liquid state can remain the ground state in a geometrically frustrated lattice when subjected to competing magnetic interactions and structural disorder.
main_result: While competing interactions can induce order-by-disorder mechanisms, the presence of structural disorder drives the system towards a glassy state, which can mimic spin-liquid behavior but obscures the identification of true quantum spin liquids.
method: The analysis employs field-theoretical techniques, extending Ginzburg-Landau theory and utilizing the replica method to average over quenched structural disorder.
model_or_system: The model considers magnetic systems on frustrated lattices (like the triangular lattice) described by coupled order parameters ($\phi, \psi$) whose free energy functional is modified by both competing interactions and spatially random structural disorder.
key_observables: The effective free energy functional ($F_{	ext{eff}}$), the glass transition temperature ($T_g$), and the stability of the ordered state ($\phi_0$).
important_parameters: Interaction strengths ($g_{ij}$), disorder variance ($\Delta$), and the ratio of interaction energy to disorder strength.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the replica method and assumes the validity of a simplified phenomenological framework for the free energy functional.
figures_summary: Figure 1 schematically shows the lattice and the shift of the free-energy minimum due to fluctuations. Figure 2 illustrates the linear increase of the freezing temperature ($T_g$) with doping concentration.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the problem of competing interactions leading to fluctuation-driven order-by-disorder, to developing a field-theoretic approach incorporating disorder via the replica method, culminating in the prediction of a glassy ground state.
why_interesting: The interplay between frustration, disorder, and quantum fluctuations is central to understanding many exotic quantum phases, making the theoretical framework relevant for modeling complex many-body dynamics.
